audit.whatIsWrong: MC_WR_TABLES.sejuani.ksante is 47.84 over 416 games; the packet says 52.11 over 190. The two straddle even and the page is written as a lane Sejuani loses slightly.
audit.why: A four-point split across the 50 line changes whether the item stages should be his or even. No rating, difficulty or side changed on that basis; the mechanical corrections below hold under either reading.

audit.why: The chart is unusually coherent for this slice — Skill at level 1, K'Sante at 2-3 as Path Maker and the Ntofo Strikes pull come online, Skill again at 4-5 and 6, then his at the item stages. Each caption argues for its own side. Given the unresolved win rate I changed nothing, and nothing looked wrong enough to need it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate mechanical errors, plus the biggest omission in the slice. First, whys[2], spikes[1] and wants.foe[1] all attribute 'percent-HP shreds' to K'Sante's passive. Riot's Dauntless Instinct text is 'K'Sante's Abilities mark targets to take more damage on his next Attack' — a damage amp on a marked target, with no percent-health component anywhere. Second, spikes[1] and wants.foe[2] call Ntofo Strikes a knockup; Riot's text says it damages and slows in a line, and 'At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in' — a pull, not a knockup. Third, nothing on the page states that Path Maker deals true damage, that Footwork grants a shield, or — most importantly — that All Out changes Path Maker so it 'no longer knocks back or stuns'.
audit.why: The All Out clause is the decisive interaction in this matchup and it is nowhere on the page. Before he ults, Path Maker is a stun that beats Sejuani's engage; the instant he goes All Out, that same button loses its knockback and its stun entirely, while his own defences drop. That inverts the whole fight: the moment he commits his ultimate is the moment his crowd control disappears and he becomes the squishiest he will ever be — which is exactly when a Permafrost chain kills him, and exactly when the page currently tells Sejuani to be most afraid. The true damage on Path Maker matters for the same reason in the other direction: Sejuani's entire plan is stacking resistances, and that one ability ignores them, so 'build more armour' is the wrong answer to his W specifically.
audit.corrected: The invented percent-HP shred is replaced with the real marked-target damage amp in whys[2], spikes[1] and wants.foe[1]; the Ntofo Strikes pull replaces the knockup in spikes[1] and wants.foe[2]; Path Maker's true damage is in whys[3] and mid; Footwork's shield is in wants.you[0]; and the All Out clause is stated in whys[3], mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly says to commit 'when his W is down' or 'on K'Sante's W cooldown' — in whys[4], spikes[2], wants.you[0], mid and breakdown.cooldowns — and never gives the number.
audit.why: Path Maker is 14 seconds at rank 1 falling to 10, and that is the clock the entire page hangs on. Ntofo Strikes at a flat 3.5 seconds is effectively always available and should not be waited out, while Footwork is 10 seconds and All Out is 120 at rank 1. Distinguishing the 14-second window worth counting from the 3.5-second one that never closes is the difference between a plan and a slogan.
audit.corrected: Path Maker's 14s, Ntofo Strikes' 3.5s, Footwork's 10s and All Out's 120s are now in mid, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1], spikes[0], early and wants.foe[0] all claim Path Maker 'absorbs' or 'eats' Arctic Assault's knockup, calling it a block that neutralises Sejuani's engage. Riot's text says only that K'Sante 'charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes'.
audit.why: Reduced damage during a charge is not knockup immunity, and Riot's description does not support the stronger claim. ksante.json's needsResearch is empty, which this project defines as unknown rather than no, so I could not confirm it either way. Rather than repeat an unverified mechanic as the page's central piece of advice, I restated what Riot actually says and left the stronger claim out.
audit.corrected: whys[1] and spikes[0] now say reduced damage during the charge. The knockup-immunity claim is recorded as unverified rather than asserted or denied.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing, and no mention that his ultimate heals.
audit.why: Riot's All Out text gives him 'increased damage, healing, and transformed abilities at the cost of reduced defences'. Grievous Wounds applied before he ults is what stops the healing half of that trade-off from cancelling out the reduced-defences half.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are his most dangerous window: he can Q knockup, W-dash through your E stun attempt, and shred your current HP across multiple trades before you can re-stack Frost. Respect every step-up he makes. At level 6 the matchup genuinely equalizes — your Glacial Prison comet can land from outside his W block range, and a hit forces a decisive trade or creates a jungler pick. Time your R when his W is down: he cannot dash through the comet and cannot absorb the blizzard zone stun. This is your best window to take a trade or invite the jungler in.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are his most dangerous window: Ntofo Strikes is a flat 3.5 seconds so it never really goes away, and Path Maker's true damage cuts through the resistances you are building. Respect every step-up. At level 6 the matchup equalises — Glacial Prison throws 1300 and Path Maker is 14 seconds at rank 1, so count that one and go on its downtime. The clause that decides fights: while he is All Out, Path Maker no longer knocks back or stuns, and his own defences are reduced. His ultimate is the moment his crowd control disappears, not the moment it peaks — freeze him then and the chain kills.

edits.before: Two tank items is where this matchup tips in your direction — not in the 1v1, but on the map. K'Sante's All Out can still isolate you, but your Permafrost armor passive means he strips his own resistances onto a target who simply refuses to die, and the moment he uses R, your team 4v4s his exposed team. In teamfights your R plus E CC chain prevents him from ever safely using All Out on a carry — he either engages into your lockdown or watches you start every fight on his backline. Play for objectives and dragon stacks; the lane is a wash, the map is yours.
edits.after: Two tank items is where this tips your way — not in the 1v1, but on the map. All Out strips his own resistances onto a target who refuses to die, and it also removes Path Maker's knockback and stun for its duration, so the second he commits it he has no way to peel your chain off. Frost Armor, not Permafrost, is what carries your resistances; Permafrost is the stun that finishes. In teamfights your R and E chain stops him ever using All Out safely on a carry. Play objectives and dragon stacks — the lane is a wash, the map is yours.

edits.after: - K'Sante Path Maker: matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1 down to 10s, and it deals true damage, so armour will not save the trade. - Ntofo Strikes is 3.5s flat: never wait it out. - All Out is 120s and removes his own stun.

notes: Win-rate sources straddle even (MC_WR_TABLES 47.84 over 416 games versus the packet's 52.11 over 190), so nothing about ratings or stage sides moved. The 'Permafrost armor' mislabel for Fury of the North survives in whys[6] and spikes[3], which I had no separate reason to open. Deliberately not asserted: whether Path Maker's charge actually grants immunity to Arctic Assault's knockup. Four fields state it as fact and it is the page's central piece of engage advice, but Riot's text says only 'charges up, taking reduced damage' — nothing about displacement immunity — and ksante.json's needsResearch is empty, which means unknown. I rewrote the two fields I opened to say what Riot says and left the others alone rather than propagate or contradict the claim. It should be settled, because if the charge does not block the knockup then Sejuani's engage into a charging Path Maker is good rather than forbidden, and that reverses the advice in whys[1], spikes[0], early and wants.foe[0].
